summary: Rulon Wells worked in linguistics, philosophy, and Indology. He studied at the University of Utah (1935–1939) and Harvard University (1939–1942), and served on the faculty at Yale University from circa 1945 to 1989.

Rupert Gethin specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Manchester under Lance S. Cousins (1982–1987), became Co-Director of the Centre for Buddhist Studies at the University of Bristol in 1987, and PTS President in 2003.

Ruriko Sakuma is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at Nagoya University. In 2015, she held posts as a researcher and director at the Eastern Institute and as a researcher at the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Ruth Fuller Sasaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago. She served as director of the First Zen Institute of America from circa 1945 to 1967 and as abbess of Ryōsen-an from 1958 to 1967.

Ruth Gamble works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD from the Australian National University in 2014, later serving as an ANU research associate and, as attested in 2016, as a postdoctoral researcher at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich.

Ruth W. Dunnell specializes in Sinology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. She completed her PhD at Princeton University in 1983, studied under Jinbo Shi (1987–1988), and served as James P. Storer Associate Professor at Kenyon College.
Ryan Anningson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He studied at Acadia University and earned his PhD at Wilfrid Laurier University under the supervision of Jason Neelis (attested 2017).
Ryan Matthew Jacobson works in Buddhist and religious studies. He completed a Master of Arts in Religious Studies at Naropa University, studying with numerous academic and traditional teachers.

Ryan Richard Overbey is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Sinology. He earned degrees from Brown (2001) and Harvard (PhD, 2010), later holding positions at Heidelberg Academy of Sciences, Holy Cross, UC Berkeley (2013–2015), and Wesleyan University (2016).
Ryodo Kudo is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a researcher at Taisho University (attested 2015–2020) and as a part-time lecturer at Shukutoku University (attested 2020).

Ryogon Fukuhara was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and Humboldt University of Berlin (1937–1941), where he also lectured. He later served as a professor at Ryukoku University from circa 1954 to 1979.
Ryoichi Kondo is a Buddhist studies scholar. He was a professor at Komazawa University (attested 1986) and later served as president of Tomakomai Komazawa University (attested 2002).

Ryojin Soga was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He held positions at Toyo University (1916–1924) and Otani University (1925–1967), and served as president of the Otani Society from 1961 to 1967.

Ryojun Mitomo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a professor at Rissho University Junior College (attested 1996) and as a professor in the Faculty of Social Welfare at Rissho University (attested 2001).

Ryoko Mochizuki is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo from circa 1958 to 1963. Mochizuki served as a lecturer at Rissho University, attested in 1972 and 1983.

Ryosaburo Sakaki worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. Educated at the Third Higher School and the University of Tokyo, he lectured at Ryukoku University (1897), was professor at Third Higher School (1899), and became professor at Kyoto University (1908).

Ryosei Fukuda, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Toyo University (1956–1960). He held posts at Shuchiin University, Taisho University (professor 1987–2007; professor emeritus 2007–2021), and directed the Kawasaki Daishi Institute of Buddhist Studies (2006–2021).

Ryoshin Nakao is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University. Nakao served as a professor at Hanazono University (attested 1998) and as a staff member at the Soto Zen Administration Research Institute.

Ryosho Hayashi was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Taisho University (1948–1952) and Tokyo Metropolitan University (1952–1958). He later served as the president of Taisho University from circa 1991 to 1995.

Ryosho Tanaka specialized in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at Komazawa University (1951–1960), where he later served on the faculty (1968–1979) and as professor (1979–2003), in addition to serving as a professor at Ryukoku University.
